questions.q: What is an Azure ML datastore?
options: A copy of your data stored inside the workspace database
A versioned, immutable snapshot of a dataset
A reference to an existing storage account (Blob, Files, Data Lake) that the workspace can use, without creating the storage itself
A compute cluster that holds data in memory
questions.explain: Datastores link existing Azure storage to the workspace. Data assets, not datastores, provide named versions.

questions.q: You have a folder of customer images. Which data asset type fits best?
options: uri_folder
uri_file
mltable
datastore
questions.explain: uri_folder references a folder, such as unstructured data (images, text, audio) or a folder of CSV/Parquet files. uri_file is for a single file; mltable is for tables with a schema.

questions.q: How do you refer to version 3 of a data asset named churn-data in a job input?
options: churn-data/3.csv
azureml:churn-data:3
datastore:churn-data@3
ml_client.data.churn-data.v3
questions.explain: Data assets are referenced as azureml:<name>:<version>, like a bookmark instead of a long storage path.

questions.q: In the lesson's local demo, why did version 2 get a different fingerprint than version 1?
options: The row count was the same but the version label changed
The demo randomizes the fingerprint
pandas changes files when it reads them
Two rows were appended, so the file's content is different from the original
questions.explain: A content fingerprint changes when the bytes change. The lesson uses this to illustrate why an edited file must become a new version rather than overwrite the old one.

questions.q: Why does Azure ML make each data asset version immutable?
options: So earlier jobs remain reproducible, since they refer to data that cannot silently change
To keep storage costs low
Because Azure cannot store more than one version of any file
So that datastores no longer need authentication
questions.explain: Immutable versions let a job or pipeline that consumed an asset be reproduced later, and give an auditable trail.
